hypothesis: The installs market is audience-bound, not name-bound: the exact name 'competitor-teardown' is carried by 15 repos, but 6 old superpowers mirrors hold 211,151 of 211,317 installs (99.92%) while 9 new clones hold 166 combined (mean 18, max 54); cluster leaders are audience-bearing repos regardless of shape (coreyhaines31 49-56% from 5-6 listings, mattpocock 41% from ONE listing of 712,820); our own listing is indexed, ranks #1 for its own name and has 1 install across 29.5h - so the binding constraint is audience attachment, not discoverability or naming. Mechanics: H78's stall rule (movers/h<20) is falsified - the 29.53h window T2->T6 carried 625,713 installs (91.6% of all movement, 21,189/h) through only 146 listings (4.9 movers/h); the correct detector is installs/hour, and 13/160 listings are structurally frozen so the effective population is 147; exact-equal increment cohorts cover 36-48% of movers globally, so H78's retraction of cycle 77 must narrow to 'repo attribution', not 'shared mechanism'.
